_about: Numeric item templates for knowledge checks and exams. Each item mirrors one syllabus worked example (module + example). Inputs are randomised within the ranges; the answer is computed by the named calc.js function, never typed by hand. `syllabus` values reproduce the worked example and `syllabusAnswer` is its printed answer; tests/unit/quiz.test.mjs checks they agree. Arg grammar: "x" = param x, "x%" = x/100, "-x%" = -(x/100), numbers are literals, arrays and objects are resolved recursively. A param with `calc` is derived from earlier params and rounded to `dp` before use.

items.prompt: A central bank raises its policy rate from {from}% to {to}%. How big is the change in basis points?
A policy rate rises from {from}% to {to}%. What is the relative (percentage) change in the rate?
A share costs {p}. It rises {u}%, then falls {u}%. What is it worth now?
items.solution: {p} × (1 + {u}%) × (1 − {u}%) = {answer}. The fall is applied to a bigger base.

items.prompt: Five monthly returns are {a}%, {b}%, {c}%, {d}% and {e}%. What is the mean monthly return?
Five monthly returns are {a}%, {b}%, {c}%, {d}% and {e}%. What is their sample standard deviation (in %)?
items.solution: Find the mean, square each deviation, divide the sum by (5 − 1), then take the square root: {answer}%.

items.prompt: Illustrative figures: world equity market capitalisation is US${cap} trillion and the US accounts for {us}% of it. What is the value of non-US equity markets, in US$ trillion?
A deposit pays {n}% a year and inflation is {i}%. What is the real return (exact formula)?
items.solution: (1 + {n}%) / (1 + {i}%) − 1 = {answer}%. The shortcut {n} − {i} is only an approximation.

items.prompt: R{pv} is invested for {n} years at {r}% a year, compounded annually. What is it worth at the end?
You will receive US${fv} in {n} years. At a {r}% discount rate, what is it worth today?
A loan is quoted at {i}% a year, compounded {mName}. What is the effective annual rate?
What is the value today of {pmt} received at the end of each year for {n} years, at {r}%?
A security pays {pmt} a year forever. At {r}%, what is it worth?
A project costs {cost} today and returns {a}, {b} and {c} at the end of years 1–3. What is its NPV at a {r}% hurdle rate? (Enter a negative number if it destroys value.)
A project costs {cost} today and returns {a}, {b} and {c} at the end of years 1–3. What is its internal rate of return?
items.solution: IRR is the rate that makes NPV = 0. Try rates until the NPV changes sign, or use =IRR(): {answer}%.

items.prompt: Using the rule of 72, roughly how many years does money take to double at {r}% a year?
A {days}-day Treasury bill with face value US${face} is quoted at a {d}% discount yield (360-day basis). What is its price?
A {days}-day bill with face value {face} costs {price}. What is its money-market yield on a 360-day basis?
A {days}-day bill with face value {face} costs {price}. What is its bond-equivalent yield (365-day basis)?
A bank borrows {cash} for {days} days in a repo at {r}% (365-day basis). What is the repurchase price?
In a repo, bonds worth {coll} are sold for cash of {cash}. What is the haircut?
A bond with a {c}% annual coupon trades at {p} (per 100 face). What is its current (flat) yield?
A company has {m} million shares priced at R{p}. What is its market capitalisation, in R billion?
A share priced at R{p} pays an annual dividend of R{d}. What is its dividend yield?
A share trades at {p}. The company offers 1 new share for every {n} held at {s}. What is the theoretical ex-rights price (TERP)?
A share trades at {p}. The company offers 1 new share for every {n} held at {s}. What is the value of each right (to buy one new share)?
You own shares priced at {p}. The company does a {r}-for-1 split. About what price should each share trade at afterwards?
items.solution: {p} / {r} = {answer}. Splits change the number of slices, not the size of the cake.

items.prompt: A price-weighted index has three shares. Over one day A goes from {a0} to {a1}, B from {b0} to {b1} and C stays at {c0}. What is the index return?
items.solution: Sum of prices goes from {a0}+{b0}+{c0} to {a1}+{b1}+{c0}: return {answer}%.

items.prompt: Shares outstanding: A 10m, B 200m, C 40m. Over one day A goes from {a0} to {a1}, B from {b0} to {b1} and C stays at {c0}. What is the market-cap-weighted index return? (Negative if it fell.)
items.solution: Total value before = Σ price × shares; after likewise; return = after / before − 1 = {answer}%.

items.prompt: A dealer quotes USD/ZAR {bid} / {ask}. A client buys US${amt} and later sells US${amt} at the same quote. What is the round-trip cost in rand?
items.solution: Buy at the ask: {amt} × {ask}; sell at the bid: {amt} × {bid}; the difference is R{answer}.

items.prompt: EUR/USD = {a} and USD/ZAR = {b}. What is EUR/ZAR?
Spot USD/ZAR is {s}. One-year interest rates are {rq}% in rand and {rb}% in dollars. What is the one-year forward rate (covered interest-rate parity)?
A US investor buys JSE-listed shares. They rise {lr}% in rand while the rand moves from {f0} to {f1} per dollar. What is the investor's return in dollars? (Negative if a loss.)
An importer must pay US${usd} in one year and locks in a forward rate of {f} rand per dollar. What is the fixed rand cost?
A trader buys {n} index futures at {entry} with a multiplier of {mult} per point. The final settlement price is {exit}. What is the total gain or loss? (Negative if a loss.)

A futures margin account has an initial margin of {init} and a maintenance margin of {maint}. After a loss the balance is {bal}. How much margin call is needed to restore the initial margin? (Enter 0 if none.)
items.solution: The balance is compared with the maintenance level ({maint}); if below, the call restores it to {init}: {answer}.

items.prompt: A call with strike {k} costs {prem}. At expiry the share is at {s}. What is the holder's profit? (Negative if a loss.)
A put with strike {k} costs {prem}. At expiry the share is at {s}. What is the holder's profit? (Negative if a loss.)
A call option has a strike of {k} and a premium of {prem}. What share price at expiry is the holder's break-even?
A company's floating-rate loan costs the reference rate + {m}%. It enters a swap paying {f}% fixed and receiving the reference rate. If the reference rate is {ref}%, what is its all-in cost?
items.solution: Loan ({ref}% + {m}%) − received {ref}% + paid {f}% = {answer}%, whatever the reference rate.

items.prompt: An investor buys protection on {n} of a company's bonds at {bp} basis points a year. What is the annual premium?
An investor holds CDS protection on {n} of bonds. The company defaults and bondholders recover {rec}%. What is the payout?
A fund holds assets of {a} million and owes {l} million; it has {u} million units in issue. What is the NAV per unit?
A closed-ended fund's NAV is {nav} per share and its shares trade at {p}. What is the premium (+) or discount (−) to NAV?
{s} is invested for {y} years in assets returning {g}% a year before costs. Fund A costs {fa}% a year; fund B costs {fb}%. How much more does fund A end with?
A company sells {n} million new shares at R{p}. The underwriting fee is {f}% of gross proceeds. What are the net proceeds, in R million?
items.solution: Gross = {n}m × {p}; fees = {f}% of gross; net = gross − fees = R{answer} million.

items.prompt: Shares are sold in an IPO at R{p} and close the first day at R{c}. What is the first-day return?
A company sells {n} million shares at R{p}; they close the first day at R{c}. How much "money was left on the table", in R million?

A government offers {off} million of bills. Bids (yield — amount): 7.20% — {b1}m; 7.25% — {b2}m; 7.30% — {b3}m; 7.35% — {b4}m. Lower yields are filled first. What percentage of each bid at the clearing yield is filled?
items.solution: Fill from the lowest yield until {off}m is used; the remaining amount divided by the bids at the clearing yield gives {answer}%.

items.prompt: An auction offers {off} million and receives bids totalling {tot} million. What is the bid-to-cover ratio?
The best bid is {bid} and the best ask is {ask}. What is the spread in basis points of the mid-price?
Asks: {q1} at {p1}, {q2} at {p2}, {q3} at {p3}. What average price does a market order to buy {q} shares pay?
items.solution: Take shares from the best ask upwards until {q} are filled; total cost / {q} = {answer}.

items.prompt: A trader borrows and sells {q} shares at {s}, pays a lending fee of {f}% a year for {m} months and buys back at {b}. What is the profit? (Negative if a loss.)
An investor buys {n} shares, borrowing {loan} from the broker. The broker requires equity of at least {mm}% of the position's value. Below what share price is there a margin call?
Three brokers trade one share on one day: A buys {x} from B; B buys {y} from C; C buys {z} from A. With a CCP netting all trades, by what percentage does the number of shares that must move fall?
items.solution: Gross = {x} + {y} + {z}; net each broker's buys and sells; shares moved = sum of net receipts. Reduction = 1 − moved / gross = {answer}%.

items.prompt: A {n}-year bond with face value 1,000 pays a {c}% annual coupon. Similar bonds yield {y}%. What is its price?
items.solution: Price = PV of the coupons + PV of the face value at {y}% = {answer}.

items.prompt: A {n}-year bond pays a {c}% coupon semi-annually on face value 100. The yield is {y}% a year. What is its price?
items.solution: Use {n} × 2 half-year periods, a coupon of {c}/2 and a rate of {y}%/2 per period: price = {answer}.

items.prompt: A {n}-year bond with a {c}% annual coupon trades at {p} (per 100 face). What is its yield to maturity?
items.solution: Try yields until the price matches {p} (or use =RATE({n},{c},-{p},100)): {answer}%.

items.prompt: Price a {n}-year zero-coupon bond (face 100) at a {y}% yield.
A bond pays a coupon of {cp} every 182 days. It is bought {d} days into the coupon period. What is the accrued interest (actual/actual)?
A {n}-year bond with face 1,000 pays a {c}% annual coupon and yields {y}%. What is its Macaulay duration, in years?
items.solution: Σ t × PV(cash flow) / price = {answer} years.

items.prompt: A {n}-year bond with face 1,000 pays a {c}% annual coupon and yields {y}%. What is its modified duration?
A bond has a modified duration of {md} and a price of {p} per 1,000 face. What is its DV01?
One-year and two-year spot rates are {s1}% and {s2}%. What one-year rate, starting in one year, do they imply?

A corporate bond yields {yc}%; a government bond of the same maturity yields {yg}%. Investors expect to lose {lgd}% if the company defaults. What rough upper bound on the annual default probability does the spread imply?
items.solution: Spread = {yc}% − {yg}%; spread / {lgd}% = {answer}% a year (an upper bound).

items.prompt: A company earns net income of {ni} million and has {sh} million shares; the share price is {p}. What is its P/E ratio?
A company's return on equity is {roe}% and it pays out {po}% of earnings as dividends. What is its approximate sustainable growth rate?
The local government bond yields {rf}%, a company's beta is {b} and the equity risk premium is {erp}%. What is its cost of equity (CAPM)?
A company just paid a dividend of {d0}, expected to grow {g}% a year forever; the required return is {k}%. What is the share worth (constant-growth model)?
A share trades at {p}, the dividend just paid was {d0} and the required return is {k}%. What constant growth rate does the price imply?
D0 = {d0}. Dividends grow {g1}% a year for three years, then {g2}% forever. The required return is {k}%. What is the share worth?
items.solution: PV of D1–D3 at {k}% + PV of the terminal value D4 / ({k}% − {g2}%) = {answer}.

items.prompt: Forecast FCFE (millions) for years 1–5: {a}, {b}, {c}, {d}, {e}. Cost of equity {k}%; growth after year 5: {g}%; {sh} million shares. What is the value per share?
items.solution: Discount each FCFE at {k}%, add the PV of the terminal value FCFE5 × (1 + {g}%) / ({k}% − {g}%), then divide by {sh}m shares: {answer}.

items.prompt: A company's EPS is {eps}. Four listed peers trade on P/E ratios of {p1}, {p2}, {p3} and {p4}. Using the median peer P/E, what is the share worth?
A non-dividend-paying share costs {s}. The one-year interest rate is {r}%. What is the fair one-year forward price?
A share costs {s} and pays a {q}% income yield. The one-year interest rate is {r}%. What is the approximate one-year forward price?
A share costs 100. In one period it will be worth {up} or {down}. The risk-free growth factor for the period is {R}. Price a call with strike {k}.
items.solution: p = ({R} − d) / (u − d); call = [p × max({up} − {k}, 0) + (1 − p) × max({down} − {k}, 0)] / {R} = {answer}.

items.prompt: S = {s}, K = {k}, {t} year(s) to expiry, continuously compounded risk-free rate {r}%, volatility {v}%. What is the Black-Scholes-Merton price of the European call?
items.solution: d1 = [ln(S/K) + (r + σ²/2)T] / (σ√T); d2 = d1 − σ√T; call = S·N(d1) − K·e^(−rT)·N(d2) = {answer}.

items.prompt: S = {s}, K = {k}, {t} year(s) to expiry, continuously compounded risk-free rate {r}%, volatility {v}%. What is the Black-Scholes-Merton price of the European put?
items.solution: put = K·e^(−rT)·N(−d2) − S·N(−d1) = {answer}; check with put–call parity.

items.prompt: Zero-coupon (spot) rates are {z1}% (1 year), {z2}% (2 years) and {z3}% (3 years), annual compounding. What is the fixed rate on a new 3-year annual-pay swap?
items.solution: Discount factors DF_t = 1/(1+z_t)^t; par rate = (1 − DF_3) / (DF_1 + DF_2 + DF_3) = {answer}%.

items.prompt: You buy a share at {p0}, receive a dividend of {d} and sell at {p1}. What is the holding-period return?
An investment returns {a}% in year 1 and {b}% in year 2. What is the geometric average annual return? (Negative if it lost money.)
Asset A has a standard deviation of {sa}%; asset B {sb}%. Their correlation is {rho}. What is the standard deviation of a portfolio with {w}% in A and the rest in B?
Asset A is expected to return {ra}% and asset B {rb}%. What is the expected return of a portfolio with {w}% in A and the rest in B?
A fund returned {rp}% with a standard deviation of {sd}%. The risk-free rate was {rf}%. What is its Sharpe ratio?
A fund returned {rp}% with a beta of {b}. Its benchmark returned {rm}% and the risk-free rate was {rf}%. What is Jensen's alpha? (Negative if it underperformed.)
A share has a beta of {b}. The risk-free rate is {rf}% and the market is expected to return {rm}% a year. What return should investors require (CAPM)?
A {v} portfolio has a daily return standard deviation of {sd}%. Assuming normal returns with zero mean (z = {z}), what is its one-day {conf}% VaR?
A portfolio's one-day 95% VaR is {var1}. Assuming independent days, what is its {d}-day 95% VaR?
A bank lends {ead} to a borrower with a {pd}% one-year probability of default and {lgd}% loss given default. What is the expected loss?
An OTC derivative is worth {mtm} to a bank, which holds collateral of {col}. What is its net counterparty exposure?
A pension fund holds {b} of government bonds that can be repo'd at a {h}% haircut. How much cash can it raise against them?
An exchange's value traded over a year is {vt} billion and its average market capitalisation is {mc} billion. What is its turnover ratio?
